subject: Fluidkey
claim: Bitquery traced at least $1.58 million in unauthorized Fluidkey payouts across six chains over about 36 minutes. Fluidkey took services offline at 18:05 UTC and is working with SEAL 911; the entry point remains unknown.

posts.note: Security incident affecting users; avoid website and app.
Reports the notice; loss not stated.
Reports no further unauthorized transactions after shutdown and says SEAL 911 is assisting.
Warns users about fake refund links.
Describes observed unauthorized relayer payouts.

subject: Wagyu XMR1
claim: About 5.2M XMR1 moved from the token's deployer address to a new wallet and roughly $13.5M was sold into Hyperliquid's order book, crashing the wrapped Monero token about 99.8%. Wagyu's operator says the deployer key sat on a previously deleted server at a compromised hosting provider and promises refunds; the key compromise is his account, not independently verified.

posts.note: Early exploit claim, ~$13M.
Asks whether it is an exit rug.
Traces XMR1 sales and about $13.2 million in subsequent ETH purchases.
Relays Lookonchain's transaction analysis.
Reports suspicious transfers from the deployer and conversion of proceeds.
Cites a CertiK flag; cause unconfirmed.
Traces the deployer transfer, token price collapse and conversion of proceeds.
Says they held XMR1 on Hyperliquid during the sell-off.
Promises reimbursement for XMR1 market makers but gives no timetable.
Reports the operator's reimbursement pledge.
Attributes the compromise to a deployer key exposed through a breached hosting provider.
Relays the hosting-provider explanation.
Summary citing CoinDesk.
Reports the sell-off, the founder's explanation and the proposed refunds.

project: Chase, Visa and Mastercard vendor breach
subject: Vendor data breach exposes Chase, Visa, Mastercard customer info
claim: Chase said attackers accessed marketing data held by vendors, and Mastercard confirmed limited email exposure in one benefit program. Visa said a provider in Asia Pacific was affected but its own systems and payment data were not; the providers and total number of people affected have not been confirmed.

posts.note: Reports claims of vendor attacks affecting customers of the three companies.
Relays an extortion group's claim that it published customer records.
Distinguishes vendor compromises from the companies' own systems.
Reports customer data exposure at vendors and says payment details were not exposed.
Links reporting that quotes all three companies about third-party exposure.
Reports Chase's statement that vendor-held marketing data was accessed.

subject: Alleged EDUTEC Chile data exposure
claim: VECERT Analyzer flagged a claim that over 10 GB of data attributed to Chilean education platform EDUTEC includes student and teacher records and photographs. The authenticity, source and number of people affected are unverified.

posts.note: Flags an unverified claim of more than 10 GB of education records and photos.
